# Tendril Design System Analysis

## Page Structure & Sections
The homepage follows a minimal, content-forward layout:
- **Navigation**: Top horizontal bar with Work, Studio, Careers, Contact links
- **Hero Statement**: Single headline explaining the studio's purpose
- **Work Grid**: Primary content area showcasing portfolio projects
- **Footer**: Contact info for two offices, newsletter signup, social links

## Typography
- **Headline Font**: Appears to be a clean, modern sans-serif (likely a custom or premium typeface)
- **Body Text**: Minimal copy, favoring concise project descriptions
- **Styling**: Mix of regular and bold weights; brief descriptions kept under ~2 sentences
- **Case**: Mix of title case and sentence case used strategically

## Grid Layout
- **Responsive Grid**: Portfolio items arranged in a flexible, masonry-style layout
- **Column Structure**: Projects appear to vary in width, creating visual rhythm
- **Whitespace**: Generous spacing around items emphasizing individual project importance
- **Container**: Full-width with breathing room at edges

## Card/Project Presentation
- **Format**: Image + linked title/description pairs
- **Text Placement**: Description below or overlaid on imagery
- **Link Structure**: Project cards function as clickable navigation elements
- **Visual Hierarchy**: Images dominate; text is secondary

## Color Palette
- **Background**: Clean white/light neutral
- **Text**: Dark gray/black for contrast
- **Accents**: Minimal use; brands' own colors featured in project imagery

## Spacing & Sections
- **Section Gaps**: Ample vertical rhythm between project groups
- **Internal Padding**: Consistent margins around text blocks
- **Footer Distance**: Clear separation with generous padding

## Interaction Patterns
The site appears link-heavy with implicit hover states on project cards directing users to detailed case studies.

## Core Messaging
Studio positions itself as making "innovation clear and unmissable" through strategic design partnerships with forward-thinking brands.

# Found Studio - Visual & Layout Pattern Analysis

## Page Structure
The site follows a classic agency portfolio structure:
- **Hero Section**: Logo, navigation, tagline "Extraordinary visual content for the world's most discerning brands"
- **About/Philosophy**: "Intelligent Beauty" positioning with book CTA
- **Work Grid**: Portfolio items displayed as a multi-column grid
- **Social Proof**: Client list featuring luxury/tech brands
- **Footer**: Contact info, navigation links, social media

## Typography
- **Logo/Branding**: Custom SVG-based mark
- **Headings**: Appear to use refined serif or sans-serif (exact font not specified in markup)
- **Body Copy**: Clean, minimalist approach
- **Text Color**: Dark text on light backgrounds; inverse for dark sections (background color: #0a0000)

## Grid & Layout
- **Work Grid**: Multi-column portfolio layout (appears 3-4 columns on desktop)
- **Card Style**: Project titles with subtitles; text-overlay or card-based presentation
- **Container**: Full-width hero with centered content sections
- **Spacing**: Generous whitespace between sections emphasizing premium positioning

## Key Design Elements
- Dark theme with strategic use of negative space
- Project cards feature: brand name, project descriptor/subtitle
- Interactive arrow CTAs (SVG-based)
- Minimal navigation with clear hierarchy

## Navigation
- Sticky/persistent top navigation: Work, Reels, News, Perspectives, Contact
- Phone and email prominently displayed
- Social media footer links (Instagram, Twitter, Vimeo, LinkedIn, Facebook, Behance)

## Interaction Patterns
- CTA buttons with arrow icons suggesting motion/video content
- Newsletter signup in footer
- Direct contact options throughout (phone, email, location map)

# Rivian Case Study Page - Visual & Layout Analysis

## Page Structure
The case study follows a standard design portfolio format: navigation header, project title ("Rivian"), categorization tags (Typefaces, Manufacturing & Industrials, Transport), followed by introductory quote, embedded video players, descriptive body text, and structured metadata sections at the end.

## Typography
Body text uses a contemporary sans-serif typeface. Headings employ a hierarchy with larger sizes for project title and section headers. Quotes are emphasized with block formatting and indentation, suggesting distinct styling from body copy. Caption text appears smaller, likely for image descriptions.

## Grid Layout
Content uses a centered column layout with text blocks and embedded media (videos with play buttons). Images and videos are interspersed throughout the narrative rather than consolidated. The layout appears flexible, accommodating both full-width media and contained text passages.

## Narrative Structure
Introduction establishes context—"the American manufacturer of electric vehicles (EV) offers SUVS, trucks and vans optimized for off-road recreation." Subsequent sections detail design process, collaborations, and technical considerations (legibility, monospace versions). The structure progresses from concept to execution to final application.

## Color Palette
Limited information visible; appears to use neutral backgrounds with dark text and accent elements highlighting interactive components.

## Spacing
Generous whitespace between text blocks and media elements creates breathing room. Quoted passages receive visual separation through indentation and distinct styling.

## Image Presentation
Media elements use embedded video players with play buttons rather than static images. No explicit full-bleed indication, suggesting contained presentation within the text flow.

## Metadata Display
Credits appear in clearly labeled sections: Client, Sector, Discipline, Office, Partner, and Project Team. Collaborators listed separately with specific roles.

## Supplementary Content
Footer includes next project preview ("Overlooked 2.0"), recent news items with dates, and contact information organized by office location.

## Navigation
Project navigation includes category filtering (search by sector, discipline), archive access, and structured footer with social links and site utilities.

# Layout Patterns for Found Studio's Perspectives Page

Based on the page content, here are the identified layout patterns:

## Content Structure
The page features a **"Perspectives"** section described as: *"In-depth thinking on creativity, technology and industry culture from our studio and team."* This indicates a blog/article hub design approach.

## Key Layout Elements

**Navigation & Hierarchy**
- Primary navigation includes: Work, Reels, News, Perspectives, Contact
- The page uses breadcrumb navigation (Home > Perspectives)

**Content Presentation**
- A "Show more articles" call-to-action suggests **pagination or infinite scroll functionality** (powered by Ajax Load More plugin)
- Articles appear to load dynamically via AJAX rather than static pagination

**Grid/Card System**
- The implementation uses "Ajax Load More" plugin with configurable display settings
- Results counter indicates: *"Viewing {post_count} of {total_posts} results"*
- No explicit card styling is detailed, suggesting a minimal or custom design approach

**Visual Treatment**
- The Found logo is used prominently (SVG format)
- Responsive design is implied through modern web standards

**Spacing & Typography**
- Clean footer layout with contact details, address, and social links
- Organized link structure with consistent information hierarchy

The design prioritizes **streamlined navigation and progressive content loading** over elaborate card-based layouts.

# Tendril Studio Page Analysis

## Section Structure
The page follows a hierarchical flow: navigation → hero statement → philosophy → services → culture → team → contact/footer. Each section is clearly delineated with distinct messaging.

## Key Visual Patterns

**Hero/Philosophy Section**
- Bold, declarative headline positioning the studio's core value proposition
- Subheading emphasizing duality: "Humble at our core. Bold in our vision"
- Inspirational quote (Bruce Mau): "Put out a pure signal, so that the right people can find you"

**Content Organization**
- Short, punchy introductory statements before expanded content
- Emphasis on multidisciplinary approach
- Values-driven language (diversity, human-centered, globally minded)

## Service Presentation
Listed as bullet points under "Our Services":
- Strategy + R&D
- Creative Direction
- Design + Design Systems
- Full Service Production
- Animation + VFX
- AR + XR Experiences

## Culture & Team Display
- Narrative-driven culture description emphasizing geographic presence (Toronto/São Paulo)
- Team presented as extensive lists of names (appears to show team members in different groupings/categories)
- Multilingual greeting signals international scope

## Footer Elements
- Dual office locations with phone contact
- "B Corporation" certification badge
- Social links (Vimeo, Twitter, Instagram, Behance)
- Newsletter signup
- Copyright notice

**Typography/Spacing Strategy**: Clean hierarchy using bold statements, whitespace, and strategic line breaks to create visual breathing room and emphasize key messaging points.

# Found Studio Work Archive - Visual & Layout Analysis

## Overall Design Approach
The page emphasizes a **news/blog-style layout** rather than a traditional portfolio grid. The content is chronologically organized with filtering capabilities.

## Key Visual Patterns

**Typography & Content Structure:**
- Posts display as text-heavy entries with date stamps (day/month/year format)
- Category tags appear prominently: "Stories," "People," "Process"
- Minimal imagery shown in the extracted content; emphasis on editorial narrative
- Headlines are concise, linking to full case studies

**Filtering UI:**
- Filter section with three category buttons: "People," "Process," "Stories"
- Allows viewers to segment content by topic type
- Simple, accessible button-style interface

**Spacing & Layout:**
- Generous vertical spacing between news items
- Single-column layout for news feed
- Date acts as visual anchor/divider
- Consistent left-aligned text treatment

**Color Scheme:**
- Appears to use neutral palette (mentions "FOUND_Logo_Black")
- Likely dark text on light background based on accessibility mentions
- Professional, minimal aesthetic

**Content Hierarchy:**
The featured quote captures the studio's voice: *"Extraordinary visual content for the world's most discerning brands"*

## Notable Features
- Links to external press features (Motionographer, Visual Atelier 8, Stash)
- Case study cross-linking
- Event announcements interspersed with project features
- Award recognition callouts

The design prioritizes **editorial clarity and narrative flow** over visual spectacle.

# Pentagram Work Portfolio Grid Analysis

## Grid Structure & Layout
The portfolio employs a **multi-column responsive grid** displaying "the latest 40 projects." Cards appear organized in flexible rows with consistent spacing, adapting to screen sizes (desktop and mobile variants referenced in code).

## Card Styling & Content
Each project card contains:
- **Image/media container** (dominant visual element)
- **Project title** (e.g., "The Wang Contemporary")
- **Brief description** (~10-15 words max, e.g., "Brand identity for a cultural center in the heart of Chinatown")
- **Category tags** (clickable links like "Arts & Culture," "Food & Drink")

## Typography
Cards use hierarchical type treatment with secondary typography noted in code (`typo--secondary`). Descriptions employ concise, benefit-focused language highlighting design discipline and client sector.

## Filtering System
**Dual-filter navigation** allows browsing by:
- **Discipline**: 13 options (Brand Identity, Digital Experiences, Packaging, etc.)
- **Sector**: 16 options (Arts & Culture, Technology, Finance, etc.)

Filter labels show closeable states, indicating expandable/collapsible filter panels.

## Interactive Elements
- "Load more" pagination button at grid bottom
- Modal lightbox system for detailed project viewing (arrows, captions, progress tracking)
- Hover-enabled navigation with previous/next functionality

## Color & Spacing
The design maintains clean white space between cards. No explicit color palette provided in markup, suggesting reliance on CSS variables or external stylesheets (`/dist/styles/`).

## Aspect Ratio
Cards appear uniform (not masonry-style), likely maintaining consistent proportions across all projects.

content.text:
Now I have comprehensive data from all three sites. Here is the full analysis:

---

## 1. Tendril Studio (tendril.studio)

### Page Structure and Sections
- **Navigation**: Minimal top bar with four items: Work, Studio, Careers, Contact
- **Hero/Philosophy**: Bold declarative headline stating the studio's core value proposition
- **Dual tagline**: "Humble at our core. Bold in our vision" -- punchy, short-line pairing
- **Inspirational quote block**: Bruce Mau quote used as a philosophical anchor
- **Services list**: Flat bullet list of six capabilities
- **Culture narrative**: Paragraph-driven section about values, geography, diversity
- **Team section**: Names listed in grouped categories (not portrait cards)
- **Footer**: Dual office locations (Toronto/Sao Paulo), B Corp badge, newsletter signup, social links (Vimeo, Twitter, Instagram, Behance)

### Typography
- Clean modern sans-serif (likely a premium/custom typeface)
- Bold weights for declarative headlines and philosophy statements
- Regular weight for body paragraphs and descriptions
- Strategic use of line breaks to create breathing room within text blocks
- Concise copy throughout -- descriptions under two sentences, headlines under ten words

### Grid Layout
- Single-column centered layout for the Studio/about page
- Work page uses a flexible, masonry-influenced grid with varying card widths to create visual rhythm
- Full-width container with generous edge padding
- No rigid column count -- items create an organic flow

### Card/Item Presentation
- **Projects**: Image-dominant cards with title and brief descriptor below
- **Services**: Simple flat bullet list, no cards -- six items presented as:
  - Strategy + R&D
  - Creative Direction
  - Design + Design Systems
  - Full Service Production
  - Animation + VFX
  - AR + XR Experiences
- **Team**: Name lists grouped by role/category, not individual portrait cards

### Color Usage
- White/light neutral background
- Dark gray to black text for high contrast
- Minimal accent color -- they let project imagery provide all color
- Clean, restrained palette throughout

### Spacing
- Generous whitespace between all sections
- Ample vertical rhythm separating content blocks
- Consistent internal padding around text
- Clear footer separation with extra padding

### Notable Interactions
- Project cards are fully clickable navigation elements
- Hover states on project cards (implicit, not elaborately animated)
- Minimal motion -- the content does the work

---

## 2. Found Studio (found-studio.com)

### Page Structure and Sections
- **Hero**: Logo + tagline ("Extraordinary visual content for the world's most discerning brands")
- **Philosophy block**: "Intelligent Beauty" positioning with a book CTA
- **Work grid**: Multi-column portfolio layout
- **Client social proof**: Luxury/tech brand list
- **News/Perspectives**: Editorial feed with category filtering
- **Footer**: Contact details, address, social links (Instagram, Twitter, Vimeo, LinkedIn, Facebook, Behance)

### Typography
- Custom SVG-based logo mark
- Refined serif or sans-serif for headings (premium feel)
- Clean minimalist body copy
- Dark text on light backgrounds; inverted for dark sections
- Editorial tone -- headlines are concise, descriptions benefit-focused

### Grid Layout
- **Work page**: 3-4 column grid on desktop for project cards
- **Perspectives/news**: Single-column editorial feed, chronologically ordered
- Full-width hero with centered content in inner sections
- Generous whitespace between sections reinforcing premium positioning

### Card/Item Presentation
- **Project cards**: Brand name + project descriptor/subtitle pairing
- Text overlay or card-based presentation (varies by project)
- SVG arrow CTAs suggesting motion/video content
- **News items**: Date stamp (day/month/year) as visual anchor, category tags ("Stories," "People," "Process"), headline linking to full article
- Progressive content loading via AJAX ("Show more articles" button)

### Color Usage
- Dark background option: `#0a0000` (near-black with warm undertone)
- Light sections with dark text for contrast
- Strategic dark/light section alternation
- Neutral palette with brand colors appearing through project imagery

### Spacing
- Generous whitespace between sections -- premium feel
- Consistent left-aligned text treatment in editorial sections
- Date stamps serve as visual dividers in news feeds
- Clear vertical rhythm separating content blocks

### Notable Interactions
- Arrow icon CTAs with motion suggestion
- AJAX-powered progressive content loading (no hard pagination)
- **Filter UI** on news/perspectives: Three category buttons (People, Process, Stories) -- simple, accessible button-style interface
- Newsletter signup in footer
- Direct contact options (phone, email) prominently displayed throughout

---

## 3. Pentagram -- Rivian Case Study (pentagram.com/work/rivian)

### Page Structure and Sections
1. **Navigation header** with search-by-sector and search-by-discipline filtering
2. **Project title**: "Rivian" -- large, prominent
3. **Category tags**: Clickable discipline/sector labels (Typefaces, Manufacturing & Industrials, Transport)
4. **Opening quote/statement**: Block-formatted introductory text establishing context
5. **Narrative body**: Alternating text blocks and embedded video/media
6. **Process description**: Sections detailing design decisions (legibility, monospace versions, collaboration)
7. **Credits/metadata block**: Structured at the bottom
8. **Next project preview**: "Overlooked 2.0" teaser
9. **Recent news**: Date-stamped items
10. **Footer**: Multi-office contact, social links, site utilities

### Typography
- Contemporary sans-serif for body text
- Larger sizes for project title and section headers
- Block-formatted quotes with indentation -- visually distinct from body copy
- Smaller caption text for image/video descriptions
- `typo--secondary` class used for descriptive text on cards (across the site)
- Concise benefit-focused descriptions on work grid cards (10-15 words max)

### Grid Layout
- **Case study page**: Centered single-column for text, with media elements expanding wider
- Text blocks and media are interspersed throughout the narrative (not segregated)
- Contained presentation for videos/images within text flow (not full-bleed)
- **Work grid page**: Multi-column responsive grid, uniform card proportions (not masonry), flexible rows, consistent spacing

### Card/Item Presentation (Work Grid Context)
- Image container as dominant visual element
- Project title below image
- Brief description (10-15 words, benefit-focused)
- Clickable category tags linking to filtered views
- Uniform aspect ratios across all cards
- "Load more" pagination at grid bottom
- Modal lightbox system with arrows, captions, and progress tracking

### Case Study Narrative Flow
- **Introduction**: Quote or contextual statement establishing the client and challenge
- **Body**: Progressive revelation -- concept to execution to application
- **Technical detail**: Specific design decisions explained (legibility considerations, monospace versions)
- **Collaboration notes**: Named collaborators with specific roles
- **Credits block**: Structured metadata at the end

### Metadata/Credits Display
Clearly labeled, structured fields:
- **Client**
- **Sector**
- **Discipline**
- **Office**
- **Partner**
- **Project Team**
- **Collaborators** (listed separately with specific roles)

### Color Usage
- Neutral backgrounds (white/light)
- Dark text for readability
- Accent elements highlighting interactive components
- Clean white space between cards on the grid

### Spacing
- Generous whitespace between text blocks and media elements
- Quoted passages receive extra visual separation through indentation
- Clear section delineation without heavy borders or rules
- Breathing room prioritized throughout

### Notable Interactions
- **Dual-filter navigation** on the work grid:
  - By Discipline (13 options: Brand Identity, Digital Experiences, Packaging, etc.)
  - By Sector (16 options: Arts & Culture, Technology, Finance, etc.)
  - Closeable filter labels indicating expandable/collapsible panels
- Modal lightbox with previous/next navigation, captions, and progress tracking
- Category tags on case studies are clickable, linking to filtered grid views
- "Next project" preview at case study bottom for continuous browsing

---

## Cross-Site Pattern Summary

### Shared Patterns Across All Three

| Pattern | Tendril | Found | Pentagram |
|---------|---------|-------|-----------|
| **Dark/neutral palette** | White bg, dark text | Dark sections (`#0a0000`) + light | Neutral/white bg |
| **Minimal nav** | 4 items | 5 items | Filter-driven |
| **Image-dominant cards** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Brief descriptions** | Under 2 sentences | Subtitle pairs | 10-15 words |
| **Generous whitespace** | Heavy | Heavy | Heavy |
| **Progressive loading** | Scroll | AJAX "show more" | "Load more" button |
| **Single-column narrative** | Studio page | Perspectives | Case studies |
| **Category/tag system** | Minimal | 3 categories | 13 disciplines + 16 sectors |
| **Services as flat list** | Bullet list of 6 | Implied in work | Discipline tags |
| **Credits/metadata** | Footer offices | Footer contact | Structured credits block |

### Key Takeaways for an Approach/Process Page

1. **Single-column centered layout** for narrative content (all three use this for non-grid pages)
2. **Bold declarative statements** as section openers, not lengthy paragraphs (Tendril's philosophy model)
3. **Services/capabilities as a simple flat list** -- no elaborate cards needed (Tendril's approach)
4. **Category filtering with simple button UI** for organizing content types (Found's People/Process/Stories model)
5. **Structured metadata blocks** for credits and details (Pentagram's labeled fields)
6. **Alternating text and media** in narrative sections, not segregated (Pentagram case study flow)
7. **Generous spacing** -- all three sites use significant whitespace as a premium design signal
8. **Typography hierarchy through weight and size only** -- no color-based hierarchy, minimal decoration
9. **Progressive content loading** rather than pagination
10. **Uniform card aspect ratios** on grids (Pentagram), or organic/masonry variation (Tendril) -- both work but uniform is more structured
